mainTopic: When חומש and כפל are owed or cancelled for false oaths about a deposit, and who receives the thief's כפל when a שומר swore and then paid
overview: This amud deals with the חומש (an added fifth) and the כפל (double payment) that a dishonest שומר or thief may owe. First the גמרא asks about a שומר who swore twice falsely, first 'stolen,' then 'lost.' Witnesses disproved the first oath, and he admitted the second himself. רבא proves from a משנה about a thief in the market that owing כפל money on the item is what cancels the חומש, no matter which oath caused it. רבינא then asks what happens when one שומר owes the חומש and a second שומר owes the כפל on the same ox. That question ends in תיקו, unresolved. רב פפא asks whether one man can owe two חומשים or two כפלים on one item, and רבא's reading of the plural word "its fifths" shows that many חומשים can be owed. Finally אביי and רבא argue over who gets the thief's כפל when a שומר swore and still paid: the owner or the שומר. Each bases his view on a different clause of a משנה, and אביי's reading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Witnesses disprove the first oath, and he admits the second
steps.stepSummary: The question ends with its final detail. Witnesses disprove his first oath (that it was stolen), and he himself admits the second oath (that it was lost) was false. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And witnesses came about the first oath, and he admitted about the last one. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing a case it started just before this, and asks what the law is. The real point of the question is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שומר swore twice about the same item. The first oath (stolen) is proven false by עדים, which makes him owe כפל. The second oath (lost) he confesses to himself, and normally a confession like that brings a חומש. The question is whether he owes that חומש too.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
About the first one (the first oath)
About the last one (the second oath)
He admitted
What is the law?

phrases.english: And witnesses came about the first one,
phrases.notes: The first oath was 'it was stolen.' The witnesses show he actually had it.

phrases.english: and he admitted about the last one. What is the law?
phrases.notes: The last oath was 'it was lost.' He confesses on his own that it was a lie.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָאוּ עֵדִים אַקַּמַּיְיתָא, וְהוֹדָה אַבָּתְרָיְיתָא. מַאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question that began just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a שומר who owes כפל because witnesses disproved his first oath also owes חומש for confessing to his second oath.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both ways to think about the case. One option: owing money as כפל cancels the חומש, and he already owes כפל here. The other option: only the specific oath that brought the כפל cancels the חומש, and the second oath did not bring any כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it the money obligation that makes him pay double that frees him from the fifth? If so, he already owes double here. Or perhaps it is the oath that makes him pay double that frees him from the fifth? If so, this later oath did not make him pay double, so it should make him pay the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard by setting out the two possible ways to understand the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that someone who pays כפל does not also pay חומש. The question is what that rule is based on. If it is based on owing money, he is exempt, because he owes כפל for this item. If it is based on the oath itself, he owes חומש, because the second oath ('lost') never brought him any כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment
An added fifth, paid by someone who confesses to a false oath about money
Frees him / exempts him
Or perhaps
Oath

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that כפל and חומש are not paid together. They only disagree about what triggers that exemption: the money he owes, or the oath he swore.

phrases.english: Is it the money that makes him owe double
that frees him from the fifth?
If so, he already owes double for it;
or perhaps it is the oath that makes him owe double
that frees him from the fifth?
If so, this later oath,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל דְּלָא קָא מְחַיְּיבָא לֵיהּ כְּפֵילָא,
phrases.english: since it does not make him owe double,
phrases.notes: Claiming something was 'lost' never brings כפל. Only a false claim of 'stolen' does.

phrases.english: should it make him owe the fifth?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָמוֹן הַמְחַיְּיבוֹ כֶּפֶל פּוֹטְרוֹ מִן הַחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two ways to understand the question asked in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the exemption from חומש triggered by owing כפל money in general, or only by the specific oath that brought the כפל?

steps.title: רבא quotes a משנה about a stolen ox
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה. Someone accuses a man from the market of stealing his ox, and the man swears he did not. If witnesses then prove he stole it, he pays כפל. If he confesses on his own, he pays קרן, חומש, and an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. He said to someone from the marketplace, 'Where is my ox that you stole?' He says, 'I did not steal it.' 'I make you swear,' and he said, 'Amen.' If witnesses testify that he stole it, he pays double. If he admitted on his own, he pays the principal, a fifth, and a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה to help answer the question. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה the man is a thief, not a שומר. So his oath is not what makes him owe כפל; the witnesses to the theft are. The משנה gives two outcomes: witnesses lead to כפל, and confessing on his own leads to חומש and an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
From the marketplace (a random person, not a שומר)
I make you swear
Amen (accepting the oath)
The principal (the item's value)
Guilt-offering

phrases.english: רבא said: Come and hear,
if he said to someone from the marketplace:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in שבועות 49b. He means just a person off the street, not someone guarding the ox.

phrases.english: 'Where is my ox that you stole?'
And he says: 'I did not steal it.'
'I make you swear,' and he said: 'Amen.'
And the witnesses testify about him that he stole it:
he pays double payment.
And if he admitted on his own:
he pays the principal, a fifth, and a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle the question from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether owing כפל cancels the חומש even when the oath itself did not cause the כפל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שבועות about a man accused of stealing an ox who swore falsely.

steps.title: רבא explains the proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that in the משנה, the witnesses (not the oath) are what make the thief owe כפל. Yet the משנה gives a חומש only when he confessed on his own, not when he confessed after witnesses came.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, it is the witnesses who make him owe double. If he admitted on his own, yes, he pays the fifth. But if he admitted after witnesses came, no, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows how the משנה answers the question. The next two steps finish the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thief's oath did not create his כפל; the witnesses did. Even so, the משנה implies he gets no חומש once witnesses have testified. This suggests that owing כפל money is what cancels the חומש, even when the oath was not the cause of the כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: But here (pointing to the source just quoted)
On his own
Yes
After witnesses testified

steps.whyThisMatters: It points toward the answer that owing כפל money is what blocks the חומש, which would exempt the שומר in the original question.

phrases.english: But here,
it is witnesses who make him owe double;
if he admitted on his own, yes, he pays the fifth,
but if he admitted after witnesses, no, he does not;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, עֵדִים הוּא דִּמְחַיְּיבִי לֵיהּ כְּפֵילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That owing כפל through witnesses cancels the חומש even when the oath itself did not create the כפל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה: a חומש only for 'הודה מעצמו' (admitting on his own), which implies none after witnesses.

steps.title: If the oath were the cause, he should owe the fifth here
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if only an oath that brings כפל cancels the חומש, then the thief in the משנה should owe חומש when he confesses after witnesses. His oath never brought the כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that only an oath that makes him owe double frees him from the fifth, then why does he not pay the fifth when he confessed after witnesses came? After all, this oath does not make him owe double. So it should make him owe the fifth!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof by showing that the second option leads to a wrong result in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the thief's oath did not create the כפל; the witnesses did. So if only a 'כפל-making oath' blocked the חומש, nothing would block it here, and he should owe חומש. But the משנה gives חומש only when he confesses on his own, so this option must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would think. Sets up an idea in order to knock it down.
An oath that makes him owe double payment
He confessed after witnesses already testified
After all; since
The added fifth paid for a false money oath (Aramaic for חומש)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. The original question is about a שומר, whose false oath of 'stolen' is what brings the כפל. The משנה here is about a plain thief, who owes כפל because of the witnesses who prove the theft, not because of his oath.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that an oath which makes him liable for double payment
is what frees him from the fifth,
then why, when he confessed after witnesses, does he not pay the fifth?
After all, this oath
does not make him liable for the double payment,
so let it make him liable for the fifth!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ שְׁבוּעָה הַמְחַיַּיבְתּוֹ כֶּפֶל פּוֹטַרְתּוֹ מִן הַחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the point from step 4 (witnesses cause the כפל) and uses it to knock out the 'oath causes it' option.
steps.raayaObject: Rejecting the option that only an oath that brings כפל cancels the חומש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the thief who swore and was then proven guilty by witnesses

steps.title: Conclusion: owing double money is what cancels the fifth
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that owing money as כפל is what frees a person from חומש, and the גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that a money obligation of double payment is what frees him from the fifth? Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's proof and settles the earlier question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the oath option failed, the other option must be right. Whenever someone already owes כפל on this money, he does not also pay חומש, no matter which oath he confessed to. So in the original case, the man who owes כפל from the first oath does not pay חומש for confessing the second oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it... Introduces the only option left
Learn from this. Here it also confirms that the proof works.
A money obligation that makes him owe double

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: owing the money of כפל is what cancels the חומש. It does not matter which oath brought the כפל.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
a money obligation that makes him liable for double payment
is what frees him from the fifth?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letter in round brackets and some don't; the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: Yes, learn it from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from step 5's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Owing the money of כפל is what cancels the חומש.

steps.title: New question: fifth and double split between two guards
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks about one ox given to two שומרים. One swore falsely and confessed, and the other swore falsely and was caught by witnesses. Does one pay חומש while the other pays כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked: if the fifth and the double payment fall on two different men, what is the law? What is the case? Someone gave his ox to two people to guard, and they claimed a thief stole it. One swore and then confessed. The other swore, and then witnesses came. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and spells out the exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that one person does not pay both חומש and כפל on the same money. Now the two payments come from two different people over the same ox. The confessor would normally owe חומש, and the one caught by witnesses would normally owe כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question he wanted answered)
In two men; split between two people
What is the case? How does it look?
Handed over (for guarding)
The claim 'a thief stole it'

phrases.english: רבינא asked:
the fifth and the double payment split between two men, what is the law?
What is the case?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמָּסַר שׁוֹרוֹ לִשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: For example, where he handed his ox to two people to guard,
and they claimed about it, 'a thief stole it.'
One swore and then confessed,
and one swore and then witnesses came.
What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבִינָא: חוֹמֶשׁ וּכְפֵילָא בִּתְרֵי גַבְרֵי, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6's rule and tests it with two people instead of one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חומש and כפל rule still applies when the two payments fall on two different people for one ox

steps.title: The two sides: one person or one item of money
steps.stepSummary: רבינא lays out the two ways to think about it. Maybe the Torah only stops one person from paying both, so here each pays his own. Or maybe it stops both payments on one item of money, which this case is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say the Torah only cares that one man not pay both the fifth and double, so this one pays double and that one pays the fifth? Or perhaps the Torah cares that the fifth and double not both be paid on one item of money, and here too it is one item of money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible sides of רבינא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the rule is about the person. Each שומר pays only one payment, so the confessor pays חומש and the other pays כפל. Side two: the rule is about the money. One ox would then end up with both payments, so the חומש would be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say...? Opens the first side of a question
The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') is particular about
Or perhaps. Opens the second side
One item of money; one object owed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule 'not both חומש and כפל' can be understood as tied to the person or tied to the money.

phrases.english: Do we say:
the Torah is particular only about one man,
that he should not pay both the fifth and the double payment;
so this one pays the double payment,
and that one pays the fifth;
or perhaps,
the Torah is particular about one item of money,
that both the fifth and the double payment should not be paid on it,
and here too it is one item of money?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן: בְּחַד גַּבְרָא קָפֵיד רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two sides of step 7's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the rule against paying both חומש and כפל tied to the person or to the item of money?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. רבינא's question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבינא's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether the rule is about the person or the money. So the case of the two שומרים stays an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unanswered.

steps.whatToRemember: We know one person never pays both חומש and כפל on the same money. But if two people split the payments on one ox, the answer is unknown (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question raised in steps 7 and 8 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of חומש and כפל split between two men stays unresolved.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about two fifths or two double payments for one person
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether one man can owe two חומשים or two כפלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asks: if one man becomes obligated in two חומשים or two כפלים, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new question. Can the same person end up owing the same kind of extra payment twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps asked about two different payments, a חומש and a כפל, on one item. Now the question is different: what if it is the same payment twice, all by one man? The next steps spell out the case and the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises a question he is unsure about
The extra fifth paid by someone who swore falsely about money and then confessed
The double payment a thief pays when caught by witnesses
A man, one person

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asks:
Two fifths or two double payments
for one man, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא's question about two people ended in תיקו, a new question asks about one person paying the same payment twice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can one man be obligated in two חומשים, or two כפלים, on the same item?

steps.title: Defining the cases of the double obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes how one man could owe two חומשים or two כפלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? He claimed it was lost, swore, and admitted. Then he again claimed it was lost, swore, and admitted. Or: he claimed a thief took it, swore, and witnesses came. Then he again claimed a thief took it, swore, and witnesses came. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what case רב פפא is asking about. It gives one case for two חומשים and one case for two כפלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'lost' case, each false oath followed by a confession creates a חומש, so he could owe two חומשים. In the 'thief' case, each false oath disproved by witnesses creates a כפל, so he could owe two כפלים. In both cases it is the same man, the same object, and the same payment, twice.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances, what is the case
The claim that the deposit was lost
The claim that a thief stole the deposit
He admitted, confessed on his own

phrases.english: What is the case?
Where he claimed, "It was lost,"
and swore, and admitted,
and then again claimed, "It was lost,"
and swore, and admitted.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, כְּגוֹן שֶׁטָּעַן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב,
phrases.english: Or else, such as where he claimed, "A thief took it,"
and swore, and witnesses came,
and then again claimed, "A thief took it,"
and swore, and witnesses came: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It defines the cases behind רב פפא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact scenario creates two חומשים or two כפלים for one man?

steps.title: The two ways to understand the Torah's limit
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the Torah blocks two kinds of payment, or any two payments, on one item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say the Torah meant that two different kinds of payment are not paid on one item, and here it is only one kind? Or perhaps the Torah meant that any two payments are not paid on one item, and here too there are two payments?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the two sides of his question. They depend on what the Torah's limit was really about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that חומש and כפל are not both paid on one item. Side one: the limit is only on mixing two different kinds of payment, so two of the same kind is fine. Side two: the limit is on paying twice on one item at all, so two חומשים or two כפלים would also be blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds, types
Money, here a payment or an item of money
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
On top of, upon

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that a חומש and a כפל are not both paid on one item. The question is only why, and so whether two of the same payment are also blocked.

phrases.english: Do we say:
The Torah is speaking about two kinds of payment
that are not paid on one item of money
and here it is only one kind;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, תְּרֵי מָמוֹנֵי אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
phrases.english: or perhaps the Torah said that two payments
should not be paid on one item of money
and here too they are two payments?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the reasoning behind each side of רב פפא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the Torah's limit about two different kinds of payment, or about any two payments on one item?

steps.title: רבא's reading: many fifths for one principal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבא's reading that the Torah allows many חומשים on one קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבא said: "And its fifths he shall add to it." The Torah included many fifths for one principal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers an answer to רב פפא's question. It uses a teaching of רבא on the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "its fifths," plural, and not "its fifth." רבא learns from this that one קרן can bring many חומשים. That means a person who swore falsely and confessed twice on one item pays two חומשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a source to answer a question
Its fifths, a plural word in the פסוק
Included, added
The principal, the main value of the item

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rava said:
"And its fifths he shall add to it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:24. The key is that the word for "fifths" is plural.

phrases.english: The Torah included many fifths
for one principal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers רב פפא's question from a reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural "its fifths" teaches that many חומשים can be owed on one קרן.

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from רבא that one person can owe many חומשים on one item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's teaching as the answer to רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבינא's question, which ended in תיקו, this question is settled. One person can pay more than one חומש on the same item.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: One person can pay two or more חומשים on the same item, because the Torah wrote "its fifths" in the plural.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It confirms the answer brought in the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Many חומשים can be paid for one קרן, so רב פפא's question is resolved.

steps.title: A guardian swore, paid anyway, and then the thief was found
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a שומר swore, paid the owner anyway, and later the thief was found. Who gets the כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner demanded the deposit from the guardian. The guardian swore, and paid, and then the thief was identified. To whom does the double payment go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It sets up a case that אביי and רבא will argue about in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שומר swore and did not have to pay, but he paid anyway. When the real thief is caught, he owes כפל. The question is whether that כפל goes to the original owner or to the שומר who already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: They demanded from him
A guardian who was watching someone else's item
And the thief was identified
Double payment from a thief

phrases.english: The owners demanded the deposit from the guardian,
and he swore, and paid,
and the thief was identified
to whom does the double payment go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about כפל begins after the חומש question was settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the thief's כפל go to the owner or to the שומר who already paid?

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue about who gets the double payment
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the כפל goes to the owner, and רבא says it goes to the שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: to the owner of the deposit. רבא says: to the one who was holding the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא give opposite answers to the question just asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gives the כפל to the person who owns the item. רבא gives it to the שומר who had the item when it was stolen. The text here only records their two rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the deposit
A deposit, an item left with someone to watch
With him, in his keeping

phrases.english: Abaye says: to the owner of the deposit,
Rava says: to the one who had the deposit with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives two opposite answers to the question in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the כפל goes to the owner. רבא: the כפל goes to the שומר who held the deposit.

steps.title: The reasons behind each view
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the כפל to the owner because the שומר troubled him with an oath. רבא gives it to the שומר because he paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says the double payment goes to the owner: the שומר made him go through an oath, so the owner does not want to hand the double payment over to him. רבא says it goes to the שומר: once the שומר paid, the owner gladly hands the double payment over to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the two rulings from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the owner is the one who decides whether to hand over the כפל. אביי says the oath upset the owner, so he keeps the כפל. רבא says the payment is what counts, so the owner gives the כפל to the שומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the deposited item
He troubled him (made him go through effort)
Transfers ownership, hands over
The double payment a thief pays

phrases.english: Abaye says: it goes to the owner of the deposit
since he troubled him with an oath,
phrases.notes: The שומר is the one who swore, so it is the owner who was troubled by having to wait through the oath.

phrases.english: he does not hand the double payment over to him.
Rava says: it goes to the one who had the deposit
since he paid,
he hands the double payment over to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the rulings stated in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the oath upset the owner, so the כפל goes to him. רבא: paying earns the שומר the כפל.

steps.title: The משנה's first clause: the שומר paid instead of swearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the dispute depends on how to read a משנה. Its first clause says that if the שומר paid without swearing, the thief's payments go to the שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about what to learn from the wording of a משנה: If someone deposits an animal or vessels with a friend and they are stolen or lost, and the friend pays instead of swearing (an unpaid שומר may swear and go free), then if the thief is found, the thief pays double. If he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays four or five times. Who gets it? The one who was holding the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that both אביי and רבא use as their source. This step quotes the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the שומר paid and never swore at all, so he gets the thief's payments. This is the clean case. The question is what it tells us about a שומר who swore and also paid.

keyTerms.meaning: An inference drawn from exact wording
Our משנה
An unpaid watchman
Slaughtered and sold (the stolen animal)
The fourfold or fivefold payment

phrases.english: And they disagree about an inference from the משנה,
as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּפְקִיד אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ בְּהֵמָה אוֹ כֵלִים,
phrases.english: One who deposits an animal or vessels with his friend,
and they were stolen or lost;
he paid and did not want to swear,
for the Sages said:
an unpaid watchman swears and goes free;
if the thief is found,
he pays double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
To whom does he pay?
To the one who was holding the deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the source text that underlies the dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who paid without swearing receives the thief's כפל and four/five payments.

steps.title: The משנה's second clause: the שומר swore instead of paying
steps.stepSummary: If the שומר swore and did not pay, the thief's payments go to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he swore and did not want to pay, and the thief is found, the thief pays double. If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays four or five times. Who gets it? The owner of the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with its second clause, the opposite case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the שומר swore and never paid, so the owner keeps the thief's payments. Our case, where he swore and then paid, falls between the two clauses. That gap is why אביי and רבא can argue.

keyTerms.meaning: He swore
He did not want to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Neither clause of the משנה talks directly about our case, where the שומר swore and then paid. Each clause only covers one action, either paying or swearing.

phrases.english: If he swore and did not want to pay,
and the thief is found,
he pays double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
To whom does he pay?
To the owner of the deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה begun in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who swore without paying does not get the thief's payments; they go to the owner.

steps.title: Each reads a different clause
steps.stepSummary: אביי draws his inference from the first clause, and רבא draws his from the second clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי learns from the first part; רבא learns from the last part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It says which clause each אמורא will read closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each clause, read closely, can be stretched to cover the in-between case. The גמרא is about to show how each אמורא does this.

keyTerms.meaning: Infers, reads closely
The first clause
The last clause

phrases.english: Abaye infers from the first clause,
Rava infers from the last clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assigns each clause of the quoted משנה to one of the disputants

steps.title: אביי begins his inference from the first clause
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the words 'paid and did not want to swear' and starts to argue that the reason the שומר gets the payment is that he did not swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי infers from the first clause, which says, 'he paid and did not want to swear.' The reason is that he did not want to swear...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts his proof from the exact wording of the first clause. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי stresses that the משנה adds 'and did not want to swear.' That suggests not swearing is part of why the שומר gets the payments. So a שומר who did swear would lose them even if he paid.

The reason is that he did not want to swear,
